title: Game Tree
body_html:
Game Tree

The tree of a finite perfect-information extensive game is a finite connected directed acyclic graph with a distinguished origin $\theta$. Every non-origin node has a unique predecessor, and iterating predecessors eventually reaches $\theta$.

Terminal nodes are those with no successors. Decision positions are nonterminal nodes. Each decision position has a nonempty successor set.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.2.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Tree of nodes, origin, predecessor map, terminal nodes, and successors.

lean_refs.name: GameTree
lean_refs.signature:
inductive GameTree
  | Leaf  (val : ℚ)                          -- terminal payoff for player A
  | Pnode (p : Player) (L R : GameTree)       -- player decision node (binary)
  | Nnode (p : Set.Icc (0:ℚ) 1) (L R : GameTree)  -- chance node (prob p → L)
```
`value : GameTree → ℚ` computes the backward-induction value for player A:
* Leaf  → the leaf payoff.
* Player A node → max of children's values.
* Player B node → min of children's values.
* Nature node   → probability-weighted average of children's values.

lean_refs.name: GameTree.children
lean_refs.signature:
def children : GameTree ι U → List (GameTree ι U)
  | Leaf _ => []
  | Node _ h t => h :: t
/-- Children of a `Node` are never empty. -/

lean_refs.name: GameTree.size
lean_refs.signature:
def size : GameTree ι U → ℕ
  | Leaf _ => 1
  | Node _ h t => 1 + h.size + (t.map size).sum
/-- Size is always positive. -/
lean_refs.docstring: Structural size, used for well-founded recursion.
